## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

# 🤯 OMG — Oh My GitHub ### 🚀 One Prompt In. A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │ └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Commit store + preview │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 🔐 Security and Access - 🔑 You do not need to create or store a project-specific AI API key. - 🖥️ You do not need to operate a dedicated build server. - ☁️ Execution happens in GitHub Actions. - 🔒 Temporary SSH and preview access exists only for the workflow run. - 👀 Review the generated commit before integrating it. - 🛡️ Restrict who can apply the `OpenCode` label in repositories that accept public issues. > “No servers needed” means no servers for you to provision or maintain. The workflow still uses GitHub-hosted Actions infrastructure and temporary workflow services. ## 📁 Project Structure ```text 📦 OMG ├─ .github/workflows/opencode.yml # 🤖 Main issue-to-project workflow ├─ wiki/opencode.md # 📖 Workflow and session notes ├─ wiki/testing.md # 🧪 Verification guidance └─ AGENTS.md # 🧭 Repository instructions ``` ## 🧪 Local Validation Validate the workflow definition before pushing changes: ```sh actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml git diff --check ``` ## 🐛 Troubleshooting | Problem | What to check | |---|---| | The workflow did not start | Confirm the `OpenCode` label is applied to the issue. | | A skill was not selected | Add a matching `skill/` label. | | The app URL is missing | Check the local app verification step and runner log. | | The PR was not created | Confirm OpenCode produced a diff and the workflow reached the PR step. | | The workflow ran unexpectedly | Tighten the trigger condition and trusted-user policy. | ## 🤝 Contributing Ideas, skills, game templates, verification improvements, and workflow fixes are welcome. 1. Open an issue describing the improvement. 2. Add the `OpenCode` label when you want the workflow to prototype it. 3. Review the generated commit and Open Project page carefully. 4. Add tests and runtime proof for workflow changes. ## ⭐ The Pitch The old workflow was: idea → tickets → scaffolding → setup → implementation → debugging → deployment. The OMG workflow is: **idea → issue → playable project.** If you believe software should start with a sentence instead of a sprint plan, [⭐ star the repository](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub) and try it.
**Built with GitHub Actions, OpenCode, shared skills, and unreasonable optimism.** 😏

name: OpenCode
run-name: "OpenCode #${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}${{ github.event.issue.title && format(' — {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        description: Existing issue to run
        required: true
        type: string

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event.action == 'opened' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'OpenCode'))
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-prepare.yml@73c5fea042dfb7c81e7f566fec2aa9c8ca8070ae
    with:
      runtime_ref: 73c5fea042dfb7c81e7f566fec2aa9c8ca8070ae

  opencode:
    needs: prepare
    if: needs.prepare.outputs.approved == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: read
      pull-requests: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-reusable.yml@73c5fea042dfb7c81e7f566fec2aa9c8ca8070ae
    with:
      runtime_ref: 73c5fea042dfb7c81e7f566fec2aa9c8ca8070ae

      request: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.request }}
      issue_title: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.issue_title }}
      labels_json: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.labels_json }}
      sender: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.sender }}
      target_ref: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.target_ref }}
      target_sha: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.target_sha }}
    secrets:
      OPENCODE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_API_KEY }}
      OPENCODE_AUTH_JSON: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_AUTH_JSON }}
      AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY: ${{ secrets.AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY }}

export function getUnitDef(factionId, typeKey, rosterType = typeKey) {
  const faction = FACTIONS[factionId];
  let base;
  if (typeKey === 'special') {
    base = { ...UNIT_TYPES.special, ...faction.special };
  } else {
    base = { ...UNIT_TYPES[typeKey] };
    if (factionId === 'russia' && typeKey === 'rifle') base.name = 'Russian Rifles';
    if (factionId === 'germany' && typeKey === 'rifle') base.name = 'Infantry';
    if (factionId === 'britain' && typeKey === 'rifle') base.name = 'BEF Rifles';
    if (factionId === 'france' && typeKey === 'rifle') base.name = 'Poilus';
    if (factionId === 'austria' && typeKey === 'rifle') base.name = 'K.u.K. Infantry';
    if (factionId === 'france' && typeKey === 'art') base.name = '75 mm Battery';
    if (factionId === 'britain' && typeKey === 'mg') base.name = 'Vickers Gun';
    if (factionId === 'germany' && typeKey === 'mg') base.name = 'MG 08';
  }
  base.key = typeKey;
  base.faction = factionId;
  base.rosterType = rosterType;

  if (factionId === 'germany') {
    base.dmg *= 1.06;
    if (base.sprite === 'art') base.range *= 1.18;
  }
  if (factionId === 'france' && typeKey === 'rifle') {
    base.dmg *= 1.1;
    base.cost = Math.round(base.cost * 0.9);
  }
  if (factionId === 'britain') {
    if (typeKey === 'rifle') base.range *= 1.12;
    base.speed *= 1.06;
  }
  if (factionId === 'russia' && typeKey === 'rifle') {
    base.cost = Math.round(base.cost * 0.88);
  }
  if (factionId === 'russia') base.hp *= 1.04;

  base.cost = Math.round(base.cost);
  return base;
}

export function unitLabel(factionId, typeKey) {
  return getUnitDef(factionId, typeKey).name;
}

The Great War

FIVE BANNERS

One continent. Five empires. Every banner answers to you.

WESTERN · EASTERN · ITALIAN THEATRES “THE LAMPS ARE GOING OUT ALL OVER EUROPE” MCMXIV — MCMXVIII

Field Manual

Command

You are the unseen hand above five empires. Every faction is playable. Click a flag or press 1–5 to assume command of that nation. Its army stops taking AI orders and answers to you.

  • Left mouse: select a unit, drag to box-select.
  • Right mouse: move or attack.
  • WASD / arrows: pan. Wheel: zoom.
  • H: dig in. S: stop. Q: artillery.

The Front

Capture sectors by standing inside them with infantry or cavalry. More units capture faster. A sector must be cleared of its owner's troops before it can fall.

Hold 11 of 15 sectors for 42 seconds to force an armistice. Capture an enemy capital to knock that empire out of the war.

War Economy

Each sector generates requisition. Spend it on five regimental cards. A full field army cannot recruit more; take ground to raise the cap.

Entrenched troops take far less damage. Shells are slow but can break a trench. Use artillery on clusters, then send infantry to take the crater.

Touch

Drag with one finger to pan, pinch to zoom. Tap a unit to select it; tap ground to order it forward. Tap an enemy while troops are selected to attack. The bottom bar carries dig, stop and clear orders.

THE GUNS FALL SILENT

Paused

The front waits. Every empire remains under your command.

THE WAR IS OVER

Victory

The German Empire has forced an armistice.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable WW1 RTS browser game where the player can control five factions: Germany, France, Austria-Hungary, Britain, and Russia.

## Requirements
- Player must be able to control all five teams.
- Must be a complete, playable game, not a mockup.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when finished.
- Responsive/mobile support expected based on repository conventions.

## Decisions
- Built a fully self-contained Canvas 2D RTS with a painted strategic-map aesthetic, no external assets or frameworks.
- Five playable factions: German Empire, French Republic, British Empire, Austria-Hungary, Russian Empire.
- “Control all teams” implemented as mid-battle command switching via faction rail or keys `1–5`; inactive factions are AI-controlled.
- Free-for-all alternate-history scenario; domination victory at 11/15 sectors held for 42s, or last empire standing.
- Added unique faction doctrines/special units, requisition economy, recruitment, sector capture, entrenchment, artillery barrages, AI, minimap, touch controls, procedural audio.
- Start screen defaults to Germany and has a “Start Game” button compatible with automated capture.
- Map/UI uses muted WW1 field-report palette, painted terrain, trench networks, flags, portraits/icons, grain/vignette.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created world/terrain generator, map sectors, trench/barbed-wire visuals, river/bridge navigation grid.
- Implemented all core RTS systems in `src/game.js`: units, combat, pathfinding, AI, capture, recruitment, barrage, victory, faction switching.
- Implemented full renderer in `src/render.js`: map, territory tint, units, projectile/particle effects, rain/fog, minimap, hover/targeting.
- Built complete HTML/CSS HUD, start screen, field manual, pause and game-over overlays.
- Built input/UI orchestration in `src/main.js`, including desktop and touch controls.
- Added procedural audio in `src/audio.js`.
- Started local server successfully on `http://localhost:3002`.
- Installed matching Playwright Chromium (`playwright-cli install-browser chromium`) and captured desktop screenshots.
- Verified start screen and gameplay render without JS runtime errors; only favicon 404, now fixed with inline favicon.
- Tuned pacing: added capital garrisons, delayed AI, reduced capture rates and damage, restricted early AI capital targeting.
- Increased unit render scale and added distant battle smoke/ambient atmosphere.
- Changed initial camera to focus on the faction’s frontline spawn sector and initial selection to nearby units.

### Active
- Testing and polish phase. Latest successful action verified camera/selection coordinates after fresh reload:
  - Germany camera `{x:1285, y:835, zoom:1.02}`
  - Selected units on screen at approximately `(740,379)`, `(793,430)`, `(667,358)`.
- Need to verify actual mouse/touch orders, recruitment, barrage, faction switching, pause, restart, mobile layout, and full match completion.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Reload/start and exercise real input: select unit, right-click move/attack, recruit via card, fire barrage via `#barrage-btn`, switch factions via `1–5`, pause/resume, restart.
2. Capture and inspect desktop gameplay screenshot after toasts disappear; judge readability and fix UI/visual issues.
3. Test mobile at `390×844`: start screen, gameplay, recruit dock, faction rail, touch pan/tap/pinch, mobile action bar.
4. Run accelerated simulation to confirm no runtime errors and reasonable match length after tuning.
5. Fix any console errors, interaction defects, or visual overlaps found.
6. Update `README.md` with concise game instructions/assumptions.
7. Stop the tmux server when finished (`tmux kill-session -t ww1`) and provide a brief final summary.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: complete HUD/start/manual/pause/game-over DOM.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: full desktop/mobile visual system and responsive layout.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js`: boot, UI updates, mouse/touch/keyboard input, game loop.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game.js`: all RTS simulation and AI logic.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/render.js`: Canvas battlefield and minimap renderer.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: painted map generation, river/bridges/nav grid, trench/wire rendering.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/data.js`: factions, unit stats, starting units, sector layout, doctrines.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/audio.js`: procedural WebAudio ambience/effects.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/game2.png`: latest desktop gameplay screenshot.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/screenshots/start.png`: start-screen screenshot.
- `/tmp/ww1-server.log`: local server output.
- `tmux` session `ww1`: running `PORT=3002 ./start.sh`.

## Important Context
- Local server is running via `tmux` session `ww1` on port `3002`; use `playwright-cli -s=ww1 ...` to inspect.
- Browser viewport currently `1440×900`.
- Reload command: `playwright-cli -s=ww1 reload`, start via `playwright-cli -s=ww1 click "#start-btn"`.
- `window.__greatWar = { game, renderer, world, currentGame }` exposes state for testing.
- Current tuning: 40 starting units total (8/faction incl. 2 capital garrison units), AI first think ≈6.5–9.3s, capture rate `(3 + power*2.4) * (capital ? 0.4 : 1)`, global damage multiplier `0.84`.
- AI only targets capitals after owning ≥6 sectors; capital garrisons stay home unless capital threatened.
- Sector threshold for victory is 11/15 held for 42s; capitals captured eliminate their faction.
- Previous idle-player accelerated simulation reached 120s with Germany reduced to 1 sector/0 units, showing AI pressure remains high; decide whether to tune further after real-input testing.
- Last known screenshot issues under consideration: map still somewhat sparse/flat, possible HUD overlap, Austria-Hungary rail label now wraps but is tiny, early toasts may appear in automated capture.
- Changes are uncommitted in git; repository started essentially empty.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.

- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.

- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.

# PlayGround

## The Great War — Five Banners

A complete, self-contained WWI real-time strategy game rendered with Canvas 2D. Five empires fight for the continental front: Germany, France, Britain, Austria-Hungary, and Russia. Every empire can be commanded by the player; the others are run by AI field staffs.

There are no external assets, frameworks, or build steps. The game is plain HTML, CSS, and ES modules.

### Play

Serve the folder as a static site, then open the page:

```bash
python3 -m http.server 3002
# open http://localhost:3002
```

The host environment's `start.sh` also starts the same static server on `PORT` (default `3002`). The opening screen lets you choose a starting empire; Germany is selected by default.

### Controls

| Input | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Left mouse | Select a regiment; drag to box-select |
| Right mouse | Move or attack |
| `WASD` / arrow keys | Pan the front |
| Mouse wheel / pinch | Zoom |
| `1`–`5` | Switch command to another empire |
| `H` / `S` | Dig in / stop |
| `F` | Focus the selected sector |
| `Q` | Artillery barrage, then click the target |
| `Z` `X` `C` `V` `B` | Recruit infantry, MG, artillery, cavalry, special |
| `Space` / `P` | Pause |
| `M` | Toggle sound |
| Touch | Drag to pan, pinch to zoom, tap a unit, then tap ground/enemy to order |

Recruit cards deploy to the selected friendly sector. Hold **11 of 15 sectors for 42 seconds** to force an armistice, or capture an enemy capital to knock that empire out. If the empire you are commanding capitulates, command passes to the largest surviving empire.

### Design assumptions

- This is an alternate-history **free-for-all**, not a recreation of historical alliances. All five empires are hostile to one another.
- It is a single-player game. Inactive empires are AI-controlled; switching banners hands the previous empire to its AI staff.
- The map is a painted strategic abstraction with 15 sectors, not a geographic simulation.
- Audio is procedurally generated with Web Audio and starts after the first user gesture.
